stem.en: Lysosome enzymes can break down proteins, fats and even damaged parts of a cell. Why does it matter that they are kept inside a membrane sac?

text.en: Outside the sac, the enzymes turn into mitochondria and start releasing a lot of energy.

feedback.en: Enzymes do not turn into organelles.

text.en: Loose in the cytoplasm, they could break down healthy parts.
The sac stops any water from reaching the enzymes, which would otherwise wash out of the cell.

feedback.en: The sac is not there to keep water away.

text.en: The sac stores all of the waste of the cell permanently, so that it never has to be removed.

feedback.en: Lysosomes break waste down, and the products may be reused. They are not permanent stores.

explanation.en: These enzymes break down the materials that cells are made of, so the membrane keeps them apart from the healthy parts of the cell.

hints.en: What do these enzymes act on?
